task_3.title: Support trailing wildcard version-range patterns
task_3.description: Conan 2.15.0 adds version-range pattern support for expressions that end with a trailing wildcard, allowing dependency constraints to match version prefixes instead of only exact versions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that version ranges accept trailing-wildcard patterns so users can declare dependencies against a version prefix, such as a specific release line or metadata-prefixed series, without enumerating every matching version.

expectation.grounded: Conan version-range expressions should recognize an operatorless version token that ends in `*` as a pattern condition rather than exact equality. A version satisfies that condition when its version string starts with the prefix before the trailing wildcard. Existing version-range operators such as `>`, `<`, `^`, `~`, and `=` should retain their current semantics.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to express version ranges as prefix patterns by placing a wildcard at the end of the version expression. Matching versions should be accepted based on sharing that prefix, while all existing non-pattern range syntax continues to behave the same way.

constraints.grounded: Only a trailing `*` on an operatorless version token should trigger pattern matching. Tokens without that trailing wildcard must continue to use exact-match behavior, and operator-based conditions must continue to use their established comparison rules. Pattern matching must respect the full textual prefix before the wildcard, so shorter or differently continued versions do not match.
constraints.conceptual: Wildcard support should be narrowly scoped to the new end-of-expression pattern syntax and must not change how existing exact-version or comparator-based ranges are interpreted. A match should require the intended prefix, not a loosely related version.

behavior: A version-range entry ending with a trailing wildcard is interpreted as a prefix pattern instead of an exact version.
A candidate version matches the pattern when its rendered version string begins with the pattern prefix before the wildcard.
Pattern matching applies to the whole textual prefix, including separators and non-numeric segments, so prefix-based ranges can target dotted or metadata-like version forms.
A version that is shorter than the required prefix boundary, or that diverges immediately after the shared prefix text, does not satisfy the pattern.
Existing version-range expressions that use explicit comparison operators or no trailing wildcard keep their prior matching behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user declares a version range with a trailing-wildcard pattern, dependency resolution should accept versions whose version string shares the specified prefix.
When a candidate version does not begin with that exact prefix, the version range should reject it.
When a candidate version only matches a partial prefix but omits the trailing segment implied by the wildcard boundary, the version range should reject it.
When a version range uses existing operators or an exact version without a trailing wildcard, it should behave the same as before this upgrade.
When a pattern includes non-numeric or metadata-style version segments before the wildcard, matching should still be based on the declared prefix.

task_2.title: Add graph-context filtering to graph-based conan list
task_2.description: Conan 2.15.0 adds a `--graph-context` option to `conan list` for graph JSON inputs so users can inspect build dependencies, host dependencies, or entries unique to one side of the graph. The graph-loading path also reports non-graph JSON inputs more explicitly as graph format errors.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan list` can filter graph-based listing results by dependency context, including build-only and host-only views, so users can inspect the relevant subset of a dependency graph without losing the default combined behavior.

expectation.grounded: When `conan list` is invoked with `--graph`, it should accept `--graph-context` values `build`, `host`, `build-only`, and `host-only`. The graph-derived `MultiPackagesList` output should include only entries from nodes in the requested context, and the `build-only` and `host-only` modes should remove references whose listed recipe or package information is identical in the opposite context. These filtering semantics should apply to each output namespace produced by the command, such as `Local Cache` or a selected remote. If the JSON passed through `--graph` is valid JSON but not a graph export document, the command should raise a `ConanException` identifying the input as an unexpected non-graph format.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run `conan list` on a graph file and ask for only build-context results, only host-context results, or only entries unique to one context. The command should preserve the existing unfiltered view when no context filter is supplied, and it should clearly reject JSON files that are not graph exports instead of producing misleading graph-processing errors.

constraints.grounded: Without `--graph-context`, graph-based `conan list` behavior should remain the full combined result set. The `build` and `host` modes should keep all entries that belong to the requested context even if the same reference also exists in the opposite context. The `build-only` and `host-only` modes should remove only overlapping entries whose listed data matches across contexts, and should not affect non-graph listing flows.
constraints.conceptual: The new option should narrow graph-based output without changing existing default listing behavior or unrelated list operations. Exclusive views should hide only true overlap between host and build contexts, not dependencies that exist only on the requested side or differ between the two sides.

behavior: `conan list` gains a `--graph-context` option for graph-based listing with four supported modes: `build`, `host`, `build-only`, and `host-only`.
With `--graph-context=build`, only entries associated with build-context graph nodes are listed.
With `--graph-context=host`, only entries associated with host-context graph nodes are listed.
With `--graph-context=build-only`, build-context entries are listed except those whose listed data is also present unchanged in the host context.
With `--graph-context=host-only`, host-context entries are listed except those whose listed data is also present unchanged in the build context.
If `--graph` points to a JSON file that is valid JSON but does not contain graph export structure, the command fails as an invalid graph input rather than treating it as a generic broken graph.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan list` with `--graph` and `--graph-context=build`, the output should contain only build-context entries from the graph.
When a user runs `conan list` with `--graph` and `--graph-context=host`, the output should contain only host-context entries from the graph.
When a user runs `conan list` with `--graph` and `--graph-context=build-only`, the output should exclude any entry whose listed recipe or package data also appears unchanged in the host context.
When a user runs `conan list` with `--graph` and `--graph-context=host-only`, the output should exclude any entry whose listed recipe or package data also appears unchanged in the build context.
When no `--graph-context` option is provided, `conan list --graph` should continue returning the combined graph-based result set.
When graph-based listing is requested against `Local Cache` or a remote, the same context-filtering semantics should apply to the produced namespace.
When `--graph` references a JSON file that is not a graph export document, the command should fail with a graph-format error instead of returning list results.

task_1.title: Clarify graph vs package-list JSON inputs
task_1.description: The update improves list-related JSON input handling by recognizing when users supply the wrong JSON format and returning actionable guidance instead of generic file errors. It also preserves correct graph filtering behavior for host/build context variants, including exclusive context modes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that list and package-list workflows clearly distinguish graph JSON files from package-list JSON files, provide actionable user-facing errors when the wrong JSON format is supplied, and honor graph context filtering semantics for host/build and exclusive host-only/build-only use cases.

expectation.grounded: `MultiPackagesList.load()` should reject JSON documents that contain graph-formatted content by raising `ConanException` that identifies the input as a graph file and directs the user toward generating a package list JSON from `conan list --graph ... --format=json`. `MultiPackagesList.load_graph()` should reject JSON documents that do not contain graph-formatted content by raising `ConanException` that identifies the input as an unexpected non-graph JSON format and directs the user toward generating a graph JSON from graph-producing Conan commands with `--format=json`. `MultiPackagesList.load_graph(..., context=...)` should accept `host`, `build`, `host-only`, and `build-only` semantics, normalizing exclusive contexts to their base graph context and returning only the packages that belong to the requested exclusive context.
expectation.conceptual: When a user passes the wrong kind of JSON file into a graph-based or package-list-based command, Conan should fail with a clear, corrective error that explains the mismatch and points to the right way to generate the expected JSON. Graph filtering should continue to respect build and host contexts, including exclusive modes that return only the packages unique to the requested context.

constraints.grounded: Valid package list JSON inputs must continue to deserialize successfully. Valid graph JSON inputs must continue to load successfully with existing recipe and binary filters. Invalid JSON syntax, missing files, and genuinely broken graph files must still surface through their existing error categories instead of being collapsed into the new format-mismatch errors. Exclusive context filtering must not include packages that also exist in the opposite context.
constraints.conceptual: This change must improve diagnostics without weakening existing success paths or masking unrelated file problems. Correct inputs should keep working as before, and exclusive context views should stay strictly limited to the requested side of the dependency graph.

behavior: Supplying a graph-formatted JSON document where a package list JSON is expected now fails immediately with a format-mismatch `ConanException` rather than a generic broken or invalid package list error.
Supplying a non-graph JSON document where a graph JSON is expected now fails immediately with a format-mismatch `ConanException` rather than being treated as a generic broken graph file.

The graph-loading path recognizes `host-only` and `build-only` context requests by deriving the base graph context and excluding packages that are also present in the opposite context, so the resulting package list is exclusive to the requested side.
Existing missing-file and invalid-JSON handling remains distinct from wrong-format detection.
acceptance_criteria: When a user loads a package list from a JSON file whose top-level structure is a Conan graph export, it should raise `ConanException` that identifies the file as a graph input and tells the user to generate a package list JSON instead.

When a user loads a graph from a JSON file that is not graph-formatted, it should raise `ConanException` that identifies the file as the wrong JSON format and tells the user to generate a graph JSON instead.
When a valid graph JSON is loaded with `context="host"` or `context="build"`, it should continue to filter nodes to the requested graph context.
When a valid graph JSON is loaded with `context="host-only"`, the result should include only packages exclusive to the host context and omit packages that also appear in build context.
When a valid graph JSON is loaded with `context="build-only"`, the result should include only packages exclusive to the build context and omit packages that also appear in host context.
When the input file is missing or contains malformed JSON, Conan should continue to report the corresponding missing-file or invalid-JSON failure instead of a format-mismatch error.

task_4.title: Expose Apple subsystem metadata in MesonToolchain cross builds
task_4.description: The update adds Apple subsystem information to MesonToolchain-generated Meson machine definitions when cross-compiling between Apple platforms. This lets Meson distinguish macOS from Apple device and simulator targets such as iOS, tvOS, and watchOS without changing behavior for non-Apple builds.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that MesonToolchain includes Apple subsystem information when cross-compiling between Apple operating systems so Meson can correctly identify macOS, device, and simulator targets.

expectation.grounded: When MesonToolchain generates cross-build machine definitions and both the build and host contexts are Apple OSs, it should emit a `subsystem` value alongside the existing machine `system` data for the relevant Meson machine sections. The Apple subsystem value should be derived from `os.sdk`, mapping iPhone, Apple TV, and Apple Watch device and simulator SDKs to the corresponding Meson subsystem names, with `macos` used as the fallback when no specific Apple SDK mapping applies. The Apple OS helper should support checking either host settings or build settings so this logic can evaluate both contexts.
expectation.conceptual: Cross-compiling from one Apple platform to another with MesonToolchain should provide enough platform metadata for Meson to distinguish macOS from Apple device and simulator targets. Users should get the correct Apple target classification automatically during Meson toolchain generation.

constraints.grounded: The new `subsystem` field should only be added for Apple-to-Apple cross-compilation scenarios and should not change MesonToolchain output for non-Apple builds or non-cross builds. If an Apple SDK is absent or not one of the explicit device or simulator SDK values, behavior should remain safe by falling back to `macos` instead of failing.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be additive and limited in scope: it should improve Apple cross-platform identification without altering unrelated build configurations or introducing failures when detailed Apple SDK information is unavailable.

behavior: MesonToolchain now adds a `subsystem` entry to generated Meson machine definitions during cross-compilation when both build and host platforms are Apple operating systems.
The emitted Apple subsystem distinguishes device and simulator targets for iOS, tvOS, and watchOS rather than treating all Apple targets as the same platform class.
Apple subsystem detection can evaluate the build context as well as the host context, enabling both sides of an Apple-to-Apple cross-build to be described.
When the Apple SDK does not match a known device or simulator value, the generated subsystem falls back to `macos` instead of erroring or omitting the Apple cross-build metadata path.
acceptance_criteria: When generating MesonToolchain for an Apple-to-Apple cross-build, the produced Meson machine definitions should include subsystem metadata for the build and host machine descriptions.

When the host Apple SDK identifies an iOS, tvOS, or watchOS simulator target, MesonToolchain should mark the host subsystem as the corresponding simulator subsystem rather than the device subsystem or generic macOS.
When the host Apple SDK identifies an iOS, tvOS, or watchOS device target, MesonToolchain should mark the host subsystem as the corresponding device subsystem.

When Apple build or host SDK information is missing or not one of the recognized simulator or device SDK values, MesonToolchain should still generate successfully and use `macos` as the subsystem fallback.
When the build is not an Apple-to-Apple cross-compilation scenario, MesonToolchain should preserve the previous behavior and not introduce Apple-specific subsystem metadata.

task_5.title: Expose Apple build-context detection and Meson subsystem metadata
task_5.description: The upgrade adds Apple build-context awareness to the `is_apple_os` helper and makes `MesonToolchain` describe Apple-to-Apple cross-compilation targets with subsystem metadata. This lets generated Meson machine definitions distinguish Apple platform variants such as macOS and iOS without breaking older Meson versions that ignore the extra field.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Apple-to-Apple cross-compilation generated through `MesonToolchain` exposes the correct Apple platform subtype for both build and host machines, and ensure that `is_apple_os` can evaluate either the host context or the build context when callers need to distinguish Apple build profiles.

expectation.grounded: `conan.tools.apple.is_apple_os` must accept a `build_context` keyword argument. With the default behavior it must continue checking the regular settings context; with `build_context=True` it must evaluate the build settings context and report whether that OS belongs to the Apple family. When `MesonToolchain` generates cross-build machine data for an Apple host and an Apple build machine, it must include a `subsystem` entry for both the host and build machine definitions, with values derived from each side's Apple SDK or platform selection.
expectation.conceptual: Users generating Meson files for Apple cross-builds should get platform-specific machine metadata that differentiates macOS from iOS, tvOS, watchOS, or visionOS on both the build side and the host side. Users of `is_apple_os` should also be able to ask whether the build profile is an Apple OS, not just the host profile.

constraints.grounded: The additional Meson `subsystem` metadata must only appear for cross-compilation between Apple operating systems. Existing behavior for non-Apple targets, non-Apple build machines, and the default `is_apple_os(conanfile)` call must remain unchanged. The added Meson field must be additive and non-breaking for Meson versions that do not interpret it.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change behavior outside Apple-to-Apple cross-build scenarios, and keep the new capability backward-compatible for callers and Meson consumers that ignore the extra metadata.

behavior: `is_apple_os(conanfile)` continues to determine Apple OS membership from the regular settings context.
`is_apple_os(conanfile, build_context=True)` determines Apple OS membership from the build-profile settings context.

When `MesonToolchain` generates a cross file for Apple-to-Apple cross-compilation, the generated build-machine and host-machine metadata each include an Apple `subsystem` value that reflects their respective Apple SDK or platform.
When the cross-compilation is not between Apple operating systems, `MesonToolchain` does not add Apple `subsystem` metadata.
acceptance_criteria: When a build profile targets one Apple OS and the host profile targets another Apple OS, generating `MesonToolchain` output should expose distinct `subsystem` information for both machine definitions.
When the host profile is an Apple OS but the build profile is not an Apple OS, generating `MesonToolchain` output should not introduce Apple `subsystem` metadata.
When callers use `is_apple_os` without the new keyword argument, it should preserve the previous host-context result.
When callers use `is_apple_os` with `build_context=True`, it should report Apple OS detection based on the build profile instead of the host profile.

task_6.title: Add cross-platform chmod helper to tools.files
task_6.description: Conan 2.15.0 adds a public `tools.files.chmod` helper so recipes can change owner permissions through a supported cross-platform API instead of handling mode bits directly. The new helper validates inputs, preserves untouched permissions, supports recursive updates for directory contents, and follows native `os.chmod` platform behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan recipes can change file and directory permissions through a public `tools.files.chmod` API that controls owner read/write/execute access, supports recursive updates when requested, and fails clearly for invalid or missing targets.

expectation.grounded: Expose `chmod` from `conan.tools.files` as a public helper that accepts a recipe context, a target path, optional owner permission toggles for `read`, `write`, and `execute`, and a `recursive` flag. The helper must apply only the owner permission bits explicitly requested, leave any permission whose argument is `None` unchanged, raise `ConanException` when all permission arguments are omitted, and raise `ConanException` when the target path does not exist. Permission changes should follow native `os.chmod` behavior, including Windows limitations where effective support is restricted to write-permission changes.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to change permissions from a Conan recipe through a supported, cross-platform helper instead of manually composing permission masks. The API should let them toggle owner access, preserve any permission they did not ask to change, optionally update directory contents recursively, and report invalid usage or missing targets as explicit failures.

constraints.grounded: Only owner permissions are in scope for modification. The helper must not require callers to provide a full mode mask, must preserve the current state of any unspecified permission, and must retain platform-specific `os.chmod` semantics instead of emulating unsupported permission behavior. Recursive application must remain limited to the selected target tree.
constraints.conceptual: This feature should stay a thin, safe wrapper around native permission changes: it should change only the requested owner access, avoid unexpected side effects on unrelated permissions or paths, respect operating-system limits, and reject no-op or invalid requests.

behavior: `chmod` becomes a public import in `conan.tools.files`.
The helper accepts owner-scoped `read`, `write`, and `execute` toggles where `True` enables the permission, `False` removes it, and `None` leaves it unchanged.
If every permission toggle is omitted, the call raises `ConanException` instead of performing a no-op.
If the provided path does not exist, the call raises `ConanException`.
With `recursive` disabled, the helper updates the specified file or directory directly.
With `recursive` enabled for a directory target, the helper walks that directory tree and applies the requested permission changes to files found under it.
Permission updates follow native `os.chmod` behavior, so Windows remains effectively limited to write-permission changes.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe imports `chmod` from `conan.tools.files` and passes at least one permission toggle for an existing target, it should update the target's owner permissions without requiring a raw mode value.
When one or more permission toggles are left unset, the corresponding owner permissions should remain unchanged.
When `recursive` is `false`, the requested permission changes should apply only to the specified file or directory.
When `recursive` is `true` for a directory, the requested permission changes should apply to files within that directory tree.
When no permission toggles are provided, the operation should fail with `ConanException`.
When the target path does not exist, the operation should fail with `ConanException`.
When used on Windows, callers should not expect executable-permission enablement beyond the native write-permission behavior supported by `os.chmod`.

task_7.title: Clean unknown-ref backup sources during cache cleanup
task_7.description: The update fixes Conan backup-source cache cleanup so cached source backups tied only to unknown references are removed by `conan cache clean --backup-sources` instead of being left behind. The change is scoped so cleanup becomes more complete without expanding which backup sources are selected for upload.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan cache clean --backup-sources` removes cached backup source entries even when Conan cannot associate those entries with a known reference and they are recorded as unknown.

expectation.grounded: When `conan cache clean --backup-sources` evaluates download-cache backup source entries, entries whose metadata `references` contain only `unknown` must still be eligible for removal if they are otherwise valid for backup-source handling. This change must not broaden upload selection: backup source entries outside the selected reference set should remain excluded from upload when an upload scope is in effect.
expectation.conceptual: Cache cleanup should delete stale backup source artifacts even if they are orphaned from any known package or recipe reference. Upload behavior should remain scoped to the references the user is actually uploading.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing eligibility checks for backup source handling, including URL exclusion filtering. Preserve existing behavior for known references, and do not start uploading unknown-reference backup sources merely because cleanup now removes them.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only make cleanup more complete for unknown backup sources. It should not cause unexpected uploads, ignore existing exclusions, or change normal handling of known references.

behavior: Running `conan cache clean --backup-sources` should remove backup source cache entries whose metadata references are only `unknown`.
Backup source cleanup should no longer depend on the entry matching a known selected reference in order to remove it.
Backup source upload selection should remain reference-scoped and should not include unknown-only entries unless upload behavior already allowed that case.
Existing exclusion rules for backup source URLs should continue to determine whether an entry is eligible for processing.
acceptance_criteria: When a backup source entry exists in the download cache and its metadata only maps to `unknown`, running `conan cache clean --backup-sources` should remove the cached entry.
When backup source upload is executed with a restricted reference selection, unknown-reference backup source entries should not be uploaded solely because this cleanup fix was added.
When a backup source entry is filtered out by existing exclusion rules, that filtering should still be respected.
When a backup source entry belongs to known references, its existing cleanup and upload behavior should remain unchanged.

task_9.title: Preserve matching library symlink paths during auto-deduction
task_9.description: Conan 2.15.0 changes shared library auto-location deduction so that when a discovered library file is a symlink matching the declared library name, Conan keeps that matched symlink path instead of resolving it to the final filesystem target. This avoids unexpected canonicalization of library locations during package metadata deduction.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's automatic shared library location deduction preserves a matched symlink path when that symlink file is the library name being exposed, instead of rewriting the location to the symlink's final target.

expectation.grounded: When Conan auto-deduces library locations from declared library directories and names, a matched library file should be recorded as the discovered path itself even if that file is a symbolic link. For matching symlinked libraries, Conan should no longer resolve the path to the canonical target before storing or returning the deduced location.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading to 2.15.0 should get the library location they actually published under the expected library name. If that published library file is a symlink, Conan should preserve that visible path rather than replacing it with a deeper resolved file.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to symlink handling during library location deduction. Existing discovery of regular files, matching by library name and pattern, and returned paths for non-symlink files must continue to behave as before. Chained symlinks must still preserve the originally matched symlink path rather than any downstream target.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only stop unwanted path canonicalization for matching symlinked libraries. It must not change normal library discovery behavior for ordinary files or otherwise alter how libraries are identified.

behavior: If Conan finds a library file in a declared library directory whose filename matches the requested library and that file is a symlink, the deduced location remains the symlink path that matched.
If the matching symlink points through one or more additional symlinks to a versioned binary, Conan still preserves the first matched symlink path instead of the final resolved target.
If the discovered matching library file is not a symlink, Conan continues to use the discovered file path as the deduced location.
acceptance_criteria: When a package exposes a shared library through a symlink whose filename matches the library name declared for auto-deduction, the resulting library location should point to that symlink path.
When that matching symlink ultimately resolves through a chain of intermediate symlinks, the resulting library location should still remain the originally matched symlink path.
When the matched library file is a regular file rather than a symlink, automatic location deduction should continue returning that file path without behavioral regression.

task_8.title: Fix CycloneDX SBOM author attribution
task_8.description: Conan 2.15.0 fixes CycloneDX SBOM generation so exported author metadata reflects the root package and dependency recipes instead of a hardcoded tool name, while preserving output when author metadata is missing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that generated CycloneDX SBOMs report the actual author for the root package and dependency components, and provide a consistent fallback when author metadata is not declared.

expectation.grounded: When Conan generates a CycloneDX 1.4 SBOM, `metadata.component.author` should be populated from the root recipe's `conanfile.author`, and each entry in `components[].author` should be populated from that dependency node's `conanfile.author`. If a root or dependency recipe does not declare an author, the exported author value should fall back to `Unknown`. The root metadata component identity and dependency component identities should remain aligned with the specific root package or dependency node being serialized.
expectation.conceptual: CycloneDX SBOM output should attribute each package to its own declared author instead of labeling everything as the build tool, and it should still produce a usable SBOM when author information is missing.

constraints.grounded: This change should not alter the presence rules for other SBOM sections such as components, dependencies, licenses, descriptions, or external references. SBOM generation should continue to succeed for packages with and without author metadata.
constraints.conceptual: Only author attribution and the consistency of the affected component metadata should change; the rest of the SBOM structure and generation flow should behave as before.

behavior: CycloneDX dependency component entries now expose per-component author values derived from each dependency recipe instead of a single hardcoded author.
The root CycloneDX metadata component now exposes the root recipe author instead of a hardcoded author.
If a root package or dependency package does not declare an author, the generated SBOM uses `Unknown` as the author value.
The serialized root and dependency component identity fields remain tied to the package currently being described, keeping the emitted SBOM metadata internally consistent.
acceptance_criteria: When generating a CycloneDX SBOM for a package whose recipe declares an author, the root `metadata.component.author` should equal that declared author.
When generating a CycloneDX SBOM for dependencies whose recipes declare authors, each corresponding component entry should expose its own declared author.
When a root recipe or dependency recipe omits author metadata, SBOM generation should still complete and the resulting author value should be `Unknown` for that package.
When the SBOM contains both root metadata and dependency components, each emitted component identity should correspond to the package entry it describes.

task_11.title: Warn on deprecated recipes in dependency graphs
task_11.description: Conan 2.15.0 adds a user-visible warning when an operation resolves a dependency graph containing packages whose recipes are marked as deprecated. This improves deprecation visibility without changing graph resolution into a failure.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan visibly warns users when a dependency graph includes packages coming from recipes marked with the `deprecated` attribute.

expectation.grounded: When deprecated packages are detected while printing the dependency graph, Conan should emit an additional warning tagged at risk level to indicate that deprecated packages are present in the graph. The behavior is tied to recipe deprecation declared through the public `deprecated` attribute and augments normal graph reporting rather than replacing it.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be explicitly notified whenever a resolved dependency graph contains deprecated packages, so deprecation status is clear during normal CLI workflows.

constraints.grounded: The added signal should remain a warning, not an error or resolution blocker. No additional deprecated-packages warning should be emitted when the graph contains no deprecated packages, and normal dependency-graph output should continue to be produced.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve visibility of deprecated dependencies without breaking successful operations or adding noise to graphs that are not affected.

behavior: Dependency-graph output now emits a graph-level warning when one or more resolved packages come from recipes marked as deprecated.
The new deprecated-packages signal is surfaced as a warning with risk severity rather than as an exception or hard failure.
Graphs that do not contain deprecated packages do not produce this additional warning.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan operation prints a dependency graph that includes at least one package from a recipe using the `deprecated` attribute, it should show a warning indicating that deprecated packages exist in the graph.
When that warning is shown, the operation should still continue with its normal graph/report output instead of failing solely because a package is deprecated.
When a dependency graph contains no deprecated packages, it should not show the additional deprecated-packages warning.
The deprecated-packages notification should be presented as a warning-level risk signal in CLI output.

task_12.title: Shorten generator-relative dependency paths
task_12.description: Conan 2.15.0 updates generator path emission so generated dependency metadata prefers the shortest valid path relative to the generators folder. This improves nested build and deploy layouts while preserving existing behavior when a safe relative path cannot be formed.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that generated dependency and build-integration files use the shortest valid relative path to referenced package or deploy locations when the generators folder is nested, instead of emitting unnecessarily long path references.

expectation.grounded: When Conan generator output needs to reference another location under the same absolute base generators tree, `relativize_path()` should compute that reference relative to `conanfile.generators_folder` and prefix it with the generator placeholder, so generator consumers such as `MSBuildDeps` resolve shorter relative paths when possible. If the base generators folder is unavailable, not absolute, or the path cannot be relativized across roots, the original path should remain unchanged. `MSBuildDeps` should preserve native separator formatting in its emitted path values.
expectation.conceptual: Generated Conan build files should prefer the shortest correct relative path from the generator output location to package or deploy folders. If a safe relative path cannot be determined, Conan should keep the existing path rather than emit an invalid one.

constraints.grounded: Only rewrite a path when the referenced path, the generators folder, and the base generators folder share a valid common absolute root that allows relative resolution. Do not alter paths that cannot be safely related, and do not normalize separator style for `MSBuildDeps` output.
constraints.conceptual: Shorten paths only when doing so is safe and unambiguous. Keep current behavior for layouts that do not support a valid relative path, and preserve format-specific path conventions.

behavior: Generator path rewriting now derives relative references from the actual generators folder, which produces shorter paths for nested generator layouts.
When the referenced location is inside the same base generators tree, generated files use a shorter placeholder-prefixed relative path to that location.
When no valid relative path can be formed, generator output preserves the original path instead of emitting a broken relative reference.
`MSBuildDeps` emits the shortened relative root-folder reference while keeping its native path separator style.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan project uses a nested generators folder and generated dependency metadata references a package or deploy folder under the same base tree, the generated file should point to that location using a shorter relative path from the generator file location.

When `MSBuildDeps` generates props files for such a layout, the package root reference should resolve through the shortened relative path without changing the expected separator style for that format.
When the base generators folder is missing, not absolute, or on an incompatible path root, Conan should keep the original path in generated output rather than produce an invalid relative path.

task_10.title: Move CLI-facing graph, remote lookup, and runner support onto ConanAPI
task_10.description: Conan 2.15.0 moves several CLI-adjacent behaviors behind public ConanAPI entry points so callers do not need private imports for remote package lookup, outdated dependency discovery, or runner resolution. It also removes the deprecated legacy graph object from HTML/DOT graph template rendering, so custom templates must rely on serialized dependency graph data.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.15.0 uses supported ConanAPI entry points for CLI-related package listing, outdated dependency inspection, and runner selection instead of private internals. Ensure that custom graph output templates continue to render correctly by consuming serialized dependency graph data and no longer depending on the removed deprecated graph proxy.

expectation.grounded: Expose CLI-backed behavior through ConanAPI so `ConanAPI.list.find_remotes(package_list, remotes)` can locate matching recipe and package revisions per remote, `ConanAPI.list.outdated(deps_graph, remotes)` can provide outdated dependency information for `conan graph outdated`, and `ConanAPI.command.get_runner(profile_host)` can resolve the configured runner for `create`. For `conan graph --format=html` and `--format=dot`, render templates with serialized `deps_graph` data and related context, but do not provide the deprecated `graph` template object anymore.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, supported public APIs should cover the CLI workflows that previously depended on private modules, while the observable command behavior remains consistent for users. Graph template customization should keep working through the serialized dependency graph contract, without relying on the old legacy graph helper.

constraints.grounded: Do not change successful remote matching semantics: only include remotes where the requested recipe revision exists, only include package entries when the requested package revision exists, and preserve the associated package configuration info for matched packages. `ConanAPI.list.outdated` remains experimental and should not report entries when there are no dependencies or when no newer remote recipe reference exists. Runner resolution must still skip nested runner environments and continue raising `ConanException` for missing runner type or unsupported runner type.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the upgrade focused on replacing private access paths with supported ones, without changing which packages are considered present, which dependencies are actually outdated, or when configured runners are allowed to take control. Any newly exposed outdated-query API should be treated as unstable rather than a fully committed long-term contract.

behavior: `conan graph` HTML and DOT template rendering now exposes serialized `deps_graph` data and no longer injects the deprecated `graph` proxy object into custom templates.
`pkglist find-remote` is backed by `ConanAPI.list.find_remotes()`, returning remote-grouped package list results that include only recipe/package revisions that exist on each queried remote.
`ConanAPI.list.find_remotes()` preserves stored package configuration metadata for matched package revisions.

`conan graph outdated` delegates outdated dependency discovery to `ConanAPI.list.outdated(deps_graph, remotes)` and only reports dependencies with a newer recipe reference available on the queried remotes.
Outdated dependency discovery returns no entries when the graph has no dependencies or when no newer remote version exists.
Remote lookup failures encountered during list operations are surfaced as CLI errors for the affected remote instead of being silently folded into normal output.
`create` runner selection is centralized in `ConanAPI.command.get_runner(profile_host)`, preserving supported runner dispatch and existing configuration/type validation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user renders a dependency graph as HTML or DOT with a custom template, the template should receive serialized dependency graph data through `deps_graph`, and templates that depend on the removed legacy `graph` object should no longer be considered supported.

When a user runs package-list remote discovery against one or more remotes, the result should include only those remotes that actually contain the same recipe revision, and only those package entries that also contain the same package revision.
When a package revision match is returned from remote discovery, the corresponding package configuration information should remain present in the returned package list data.
When a user checks for outdated dependencies across remotes, only dependencies whose newest available remote recipe reference is newer than the local cached one should be reported.
When the dependency graph contains no dependencies, or all queried remotes are at the same or older versions, outdated dependency inspection should return no outdated entries.

When runner execution is configured for `create` outside an existing runner environment, supported runner types should still be selected, while invalid runner configuration or unsupported runner types should still raise a `ConanException`.

task_15.title: Respect lockfile revisions with legacy update policy
task_15.description: The 2.15.0 update fixes a regression where using Conan's deprecated `core:update_policy=legacy` together with lockfiles could fail during update-enabled resolution. Locked references that already carry a revision are now treated as fixed inputs instead of being sent through the legacy update flow.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan operations using `core:update_policy=legacy` remain compatible with lockfiles, and that references already pinned to a revision by a lockfile are not reprocessed through the legacy update path.

expectation.grounded: When `core:update_policy=legacy` is enabled and update processing is active, Conan should apply the legacy update-policy branch only to references that do not already have a revision. For references resolved from a lockfile with an explicit `reference.revision`, Conan should bypass that legacy update branch, preserve the locked revision, and complete the operation without failing.
expectation.conceptual: Using the legacy update policy together with lockfiles should be stable. If a lockfile has already pinned a dependency or package revision, update-enabled execution should respect that pinned revision instead of trying to refresh it through the legacy update mechanism.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing legacy update behavior for references that have no revision. Do not treat lockfile-pinned references as candidates for legacy remote update resolution merely because update mode is enabled. The fix should be limited to avoiding incorrect legacy-update handling for already-revisioned references.
constraints.conceptual: Keep current update behavior for unresolved references, while treating lockfile-pinned revisions as authoritative and non-updatable within the legacy policy flow.

behavior: With `core:update_policy=legacy` enabled, the legacy update-policy path is skipped for references that already include a revision.
Lockfile-based operations no longer fail solely because legacy update policy is active while processing revision-pinned references.
References without a pinned revision continue to follow the existing legacy update-policy behavior during update checks.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan runs with update enabled and `core:update_policy=legacy`, and a lockfile provides a reference with an explicit revision, the operation should complete successfully without an error caused by legacy update handling.
When a lockfile pins a revision, enabling the legacy update policy should not cause Conan to replace, refresh, or re-resolve that pinned revision through the legacy update path.
When a reference has no explicit revision, enabling `core:update_policy=legacy` should still allow the existing legacy update behavior to run.
Using lockfiles together with the legacy update policy should preserve the lockfile's revision choices as the effective resolved state.

task_13.title: Fix CMakeDeps component type handling for shared dependencies
task_13.description: The 2.15.0 update fixes CMakeDeps dependency target generation for recipes that declare component-level dependencies. It now reads component type metadata from the correct public attribute and preserves the intended shared-library dependency behavior for same-package, cross-package, and root-package requirements, preventing generation failures and incorrect linkage decisions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeDeps can consume packages that declare component dependencies without failing on component metadata lookup, and ensure that shared-library dependency relationships are generated correctly for dependencies within the same package, across packages, and when requiring another package's root target.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeDeps processes `cpp_info.requires` involving components, it should use each `_Component`'s `type` attribute rather than a nonexistent `package_type` attribute. Dependency target generation should succeed for component requirements inside the same package and across packages. Shared-library link decisions should continue to respect `PackageType.SHARED`, including when a requirement resolves to another package's root target instead of a named component.
expectation.conceptual: Packages that model libraries through `cpp_info` components should remain consumable through CMakeDeps. Declaring shared-library components or transitive requirements must not cause generator failures, and the generated dependency relationships should match whether the consumer and dependency are shared libraries.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress `cmake_target_name`-based target resolution, same-package component dependency resolution, cross-package component resolution, or root target resolution for package-level requirements. Preserve existing non-shared dependency behavior while eliminating failures caused by looking for `_Component.package_type`.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing target naming and dependency resolution stable except for correcting the broken component metadata lookup and the resulting shared-library linkage behavior. Non-shared consumers should continue to receive the dependency links they previously relied on.

behavior: CMakeDeps no longer fails when resolving dependencies from `cpp_info.components` that define a component `type`.
For component requirements within the same package, shared-library link decisions are based on the required component's declared `type`.
For component requirements on another package, shared-library link decisions are based on the referenced component's declared `type` rather than a missing component `package_type` attribute.

When a requirement resolves to another package's root target instead of a named component, shared-library consumers treat that dependency as non-linking, while non-shared consumers still receive a linkable dependency relationship.
acceptance_criteria: When a package defines multiple components and one component requires another component from the same package, CMakeDeps generation should complete successfully and produce consumable CMake package information.
When a component requires a component from another package, CMakeDeps generation should complete successfully without attribute lookup failures and should resolve the referenced dependency target.

When a shared-library package requires another package through its root target rather than a specific component, the generated dependency relationship should avoid treating that requirement as a direct linkable shared component dependency.
When the depending package is not a shared library, requiring another package's root target should continue to produce a linkable dependency relationship.

task_14.title: Fix global.conf and profile [conf] precedence
task_14.description: Configuration composition was corrected so values from global.conf behave as shared defaults instead of overriding profile-level [conf] settings. The update also fixes the effective ordering of per-package pattern configuration entries so profile-specific overrides and ordered list composition behave consistently when both global and profile sources define the same scope.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that configuration values defined in global.conf do not take precedence over profile [conf] values, and ensure that per-package pattern configuration inherited from global.conf is applied in an order that lets profile-specific package configuration override or extend it predictably.

expectation.grounded: When Conan combines global.conf with a profile [conf] section, global.conf must be treated as the base ConfDefinition and the profile must be layered on top of it. Plain configuration keys defined in both places must resolve to the profile value. Pattern-scoped entries, including package-specific patterns such as the consumer pattern and other per-package patterns, must preserve global definitions as defaults while composing profile pattern definitions afterward, so later profile assignments override earlier global assignments and profile append or prepend style list operations are evaluated relative to inherited global values.
expectation.conceptual: Global configuration should supply defaults, not win conflicts. If the same configuration is declared globally and in a profile, the profile should determine the effective result. Package-scoped configuration coming from the global level should still be inherited, but profile package rules should be applied after it so overrides and ordered value composition match user intent.

constraints.grounded: Do not drop unrelated global.conf entries when combining with a profile. Pattern entries that exist only in global.conf must remain active after composition, and profile-only entries must continue to work unchanged. The fix must change precedence and ordering between global and profile sources without altering the meaning of standalone global.conf usage or standalone profile [conf] usage.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve all independent configuration that does not conflict, and limit the change to how global and profile settings are merged. Existing behavior for configurations defined in only one source should remain intact.

behavior: A profile [conf] value overrides the same non-pattern configuration key coming from global.conf.
Per-package or pattern-scoped configuration from global.conf is retained as inherited baseline configuration when a profile is applied.

When the same package pattern and key are defined in both global.conf and a profile, the effective composition order is global first and profile second, making the profile the higher-precedence source.

Ordered collection-style configuration operations on pattern-scoped values follow the same precedence model, so profile-side append or prepend operations are applied relative to the globally inherited value set rather than being replaced or evaluated in the wrong order.
acceptance_criteria: When a configuration key is defined in both global.conf and a profile [conf], Conan should resolve the effective value from the profile.

When global.conf defines package-scoped configuration and the profile defines different package-scoped configuration, the global entries should still be inherited and the profile entries should also remain effective for their scopes.
When global.conf and the profile both define the same package-scoped configuration key, the profile definition should take precedence in the final resolved behavior.

When package-scoped list-like configuration is combined across global and profile sources, append or prepend semantics should reflect global defaults being applied before profile-specific modifications.

task_18.title: Fix JSON output for class-based custom tool generators
task_18.description: Version 2.15.0 fixes a crash in JSON-formatted Conan output when a tool requirement exposes a custom generator by class reference instead of by string name. JSON serialization should now complete successfully and report generator names in a stable, user-readable form.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan JSON output does not crash when a tool-require provides a custom generator as a class reference instead of a string name, and that the serialized generator list remains readable and usable to clients consuming `--format=json` output.

expectation.grounded: When Conan serializes recipe metadata for `--format=json`, any entries in the exposed `generators` collection that are Python class objects from custom tool-require generators must be represented by their class names. Serialization must succeed for tool requirements that publish custom generators by class reference rather than by string name.
expectation.conceptual: JSON-formatted Conan output should support custom generators from tool packages regardless of whether they were declared by name or by class, and it should present those generators as normal names instead of failing.

constraints.grounded: String-based generator declarations must continue to serialize unchanged. The `generators` field must remain a list in JSON output, and class-based entries must be converted into stable string names instead of exposing non-serializable class objects or causing serialization errors.
constraints.conceptual: Existing JSON consumers should continue receiving the same overall generator list structure, with the only change being that previously failing class-based custom generators now appear as names and do not break output generation.

behavior: Conan no longer crashes while producing `--format=json` output when a tool requirement contributes a custom generator via a class reference.
The JSON `generators` field continues to be emitted as a list.
If a generator entry is already a string name, it is preserved as-is in the serialized output.
If a generator entry is provided as a class object, the serialized output contains that class's name rather than the raw class object.
acceptance_criteria: When a tool-require exposes a custom generator as a class and Conan output is requested with `--format=json`, the command should complete successfully without a serialization failure.
When JSON output includes generators originating from tool requirements, class-based custom generators should appear by name in the `generators` list.
When generators are declared by string name, `--format=json` should keep returning those names without changing the JSON field shape.
When a client consumes the JSON graph or recipe metadata, the `generators` field should remain consistently parseable as a list of names.

task_16.title: Fix untargz extraction for restrictive directory modes
task_16.description: The upgrade fixes a regression in tar extraction so archives containing directories with restrictive stored permissions can be unpacked successfully, including selective extraction scenarios such as root stripping. As part of this change, callers should no longer expect percentage-style extraction progress reporting from `untargz()` in this version.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `untargz()` can extract tar archives even when archived directories have restrictive permission modes, including during selective extraction flows such as `strip_root` and pattern-based extraction, without requiring callers to modify the archive or relax permissions first.

expectation.grounded: `untargz(filename, destination=".", pattern=None, strip_root=False, extract_filter=None)` should complete extraction without failing solely because directory entries inside the archive carry restrictive modes. This should remain true for full extraction and for extractions that use `pattern`, `strip_root`, and `extract_filter`, while preserving the current member-selection and root-stripping behavior. Percentage-style progress reporting during `untargz()` extraction is not part of the expected behavior in this release.
expectation.conceptual: Tar extraction should succeed for valid archives even if some archived folders are marked with restrictive permissions. Optional filtering and root-stripping features should continue to work the same way from the caller’s perspective, and users should not depend on percentage progress updates during extraction.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable selection semantics of `pattern`, `strip_root`, or `extract_filter`. Do not introduce a requirement for users to pre-adjust archive permissions. Existing invalid-root handling for `strip_root` must remain intact. The fix should address permission-related extraction failures without redefining archive contents or extraction targets.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should remove the permission-related failure mode without changing which files are extracted, how root stripping behaves, or how archive filtering works. It should preserve existing validation behavior for unsupported archive layouts.

behavior: `untargz()` no longer fails with permission-related extraction errors when the archive contains directory entries whose stored modes are more restrictive than their descendants require.
This corrected behavior applies to selective extraction paths as well as full extraction, including calls that use `strip_root=True` or a `pattern` filter.
When `extract_filter` is supplied, extraction still honors that filtering stage while avoiding the restrictive-directory failure mode.
Users should not rely on percentage-based extraction progress output from `untargz()` in 2.15.0.
acceptance_criteria: When `untargz()` extracts a valid tar archive that contains nested directories with restrictive permission modes, it should finish without a permission-related exception and materialize the expected files under the destination.
When the same kind of archive is extracted with `strip_root=True`, extraction should still succeed without permission-related failure and should produce the stripped-root layout.
When a `pattern` is provided, `untargz()` should extract only matching members while remaining resilient to restrictive directory modes elsewhere in the selected extraction path.
When `extract_filter` is provided, `untargz()` should continue to apply the filter and still avoid failing solely because archived directories are restrictive.
During `untargz()` execution, absence of percentage-style progress feedback should be considered acceptable behavior for this release.

task_17.title: Prioritize exact library filename matches in CppInfo auto-deduction
task_17.description: The 2.15.0 update fixes library auto-detection so Conan prefers an exact library filename match before considering similarly named variants. This avoids resolving the wrong artifact when both the requested library and related suffixed libraries are present, while preserving fallback support for versioned or otherwise qualified library filenames.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's automatic C/C++ library location deduction prefers the exact library requested by `cpp_info.libs` before matching similarly named library files, so packages resolve the intended artifact when exact and suffixed library names coexist.

expectation.grounded: When `CppInfo.auto_deduce_location` resolves libraries declared in `cpp_info.libs`, it should first look for exact static or shared library filenames whose basename matches the declared library name, allowing the conventional `lib` prefix and standard platform extensions. Only if no exact static/shared match is found should it broaden the search to compatible filenames that append additional segments separated by `.`, `_`, or `-`. The existing DLL-side lookup behavior should remain compatible with the resolved library selection.
expectation.conceptual: Library auto-detection should choose the exact requested library whenever it is available, and only fall back to close-name variants when no exact match exists.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress support for Unix-style `lib` prefixes or for suffixed/versioned static and shared library filenames when an exact basename is absent. Do not broaden matching beyond the existing accepted filename families; this change is only about prioritization of exact matches over wider matches.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped: keep current compatibility with normal library naming conventions and fallback matching, but remove incorrect preference for similarly named libraries over the exact one.

behavior: Exact static library filenames matching the declared library name are prioritized over similarly named static libraries with extra suffix segments.
Exact shared library filenames matching the declared library name are prioritized over similarly named shared libraries with extra suffix segments.
If no exact static or shared library filename exists, auto-deduction still falls back to compatible suffixed or versioned library filenames.
Conventional `lib`-prefixed filenames remain eligible under the same exact-match-first behavior.
Windows DLL companion resolution remains aligned with the selected library rather than changing matching scope for DLL discovery.
acceptance_criteria: When a declared library name has both an exact library file and one or more similarly named suffixed library files available, auto-deduction should resolve the exact library file.
When an exact shared library file exists alongside versioned or otherwise suffixed shared library files for the same declared name, the exact shared library should be selected.
When an exact static library file exists alongside suffixed static library files for the same declared name, the exact static library should be selected.

When no exact basename match exists but a compatible suffixed or versioned library file does exist, auto-deduction should still resolve a matching library instead of failing solely because the exact filename is absent.
When the available exact-match library uses the conventional `lib` prefix, it should still be preferred over broader filename matches.

task_19.title: Fix CycloneDX SBOM metadata and empty-component generation
task_19.description: Conan 2.15.0 fixes CycloneDX SBOM generation so the metadata section describes the root Conanfile or package with the correct author and package reference, and SBOM creation no longer crashes when graph filtering leaves no component associated with a special root node.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CycloneDX SBOM generation reports correct metadata for the package or consumer being described and still succeeds when the resolved graph produces no emitted components after root-node and context filtering.

expectation.grounded: `conan.tools.sbom.cyclonedx.cyclonedx_1_4()` should populate `metadata.component` from the root `conanfile` rather than from a dependency node, including the root package reference used for `bom-ref` and the declared author metadata when available. Generated `components` entries should likewise expose author information from each package recipe instead of a generic tool author. If host/build/test filtering and special-root-node handling leave zero included nodes, SBOM generation should still return a valid CycloneDX document with `metadata`, omitting `components` when empty instead of raising an exception.
expectation.conceptual: When a CycloneDX SBOM is generated, the top-level metadata should describe the actual package or consumer that requested the SBOM, not one of its dependencies. Package author details should come from package metadata when available. SBOM generation must also work for edge cases where the filtered dependency graph contributes no output components.

constraints.grounded: Existing filtering semantics for `add_build`, `add_tests`, and special root-node dependency handling should remain intact. The fix must not fabricate placeholder components solely to avoid failure; an empty component set is allowed as long as the document is still emitted with valid metadata and any applicable dependency relationships.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the current inclusion rules for build and test dependencies, and preserve normal dependency reporting behavior. If there is nothing to list as a component, the SBOM should still be generated cleanly without inventing extra package entries.

behavior: CycloneDX `metadata.component.author` now reflects the root Conanfile's declared author information instead of a generic tool value.
CycloneDX `metadata.component.bom-ref` now identifies the root package or consumer reference rather than reusing a dependency component reference.
Each emitted SBOM component now reports author information from that component's recipe metadata when available.

When special-root-node processing and build/test/context filtering produce zero emitted components, SBOM generation completes successfully and returns a document without a `components` section instead of crashing.
acceptance_criteria: When generating a CycloneDX SBOM for a package with declared author metadata, the top-level `metadata.component` should identify that package and expose its author information.
When generating a CycloneDX SBOM for a dependency graph with multiple packages, the top-level `metadata.component.bom-ref` should point to the root package or consumer rather than a dependency entry.
When emitted components correspond to package recipes that declare author metadata, each component entry should expose that author information in the SBOM output.

Given a graph where special root-node handling and current filter options leave no included components, generating the CycloneDX SBOM should still succeed and produce valid metadata instead of failing.
